liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Creepy version with a very long quiet passage that tempts listeners to hold their breath; Unusually fast pace for 1970, funky Phil throughout, Coltrane-like Garcia runs after 14:00, and Bobby halts the band abruptly around 19:00 [11][12]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Phil's introduction leads into The Other One, followed by a tasty Dark Star [9]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Reviewer agrees with the Taper's Compendium suspicion that this GDTRFB comes from another show, citing a tonal difference [11]

## The recordings

- **gd70-11-05.aud.warner.17182.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 14 songs; 112 min; rated 4.29/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience tape with rumbly Phil bass; otherwise sounds good for 1970 and improves if bass is turned down; Bass end is badly distorted, though this is said to be the best available recording [7][14]
- **gd1970-11-05.aud.lee.sirmick.30115.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 13 songs; 112 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1970-11-05.aud.harlan.9356.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 9 songs; 75 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- Show started with Hard to Handle after a delay to replace a string [9]
- Attendee in the tenth row center remembers a powerhouse performance with a huge band tone the tapes fail to capture [15]
- Lacks the Pigpen showcase of the next night and the rarities of 11/8, but is a solid, unadorned 1970 show [4]
- Reviewer wishes soundboards existed for this November run; the 8th is well circulated, and the 7th would get more mention if better sounding [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-11-05.aud.warner.17182.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Ken Leigh; transferred by Jack Warner; source: Audience [1]. Also: Older lower-generation tapes labeled 11/7/70 actually joined the 11/5 Not Fade Away jam to the 11/6 Alligator/NFA at the cut; Recorded by Ken Leigh on a Sony TC-110 with built-in mic from center loge; mastered by Jack Warner; Tape flip between D2T2 and D2T3 was cross-faded; Drums is tracked so it can be skipped [1][8]
- **gd1970-11-05.aud.lee.sirmick.30115.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ken Leigh; transferred by SirMick; source: Recorded by Ken Leigh with a Sony TC-110 with built-in microphone, from center loge [2]
- **gd1970-11-05.aud.harlan.9356.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Harlan; source: center lodge, mics mounted on rails->Sony cassette audience master-> analog cassette XL II, no dolby->Sony TC D5M DAT->playback on Sony PCM R-700-> HDD via… [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Rock Candy Posters: [GRATEFUL DEAD - CAPITOL THEATER 1970 - POSTER - AJ MASTAHY](https://www.rockcandyposters.com/grateful-dead-capitol-theater-1970-poster-aj-mastahy/) [17]
- Fan art by Rock Candy Posters: [GRATEFUL DEAD - CAPITOL THEATER 1970 - POSTER - AJ MASTAHY](https://www.rockcandyposters.com/grateful-dead-capitol-theater-1970-poster-aj-mastahy/) [18]
